newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Rains raise prospects for 5 pct EU farm set-aside.
newsitem.headline: Rains raise prospects for 5 pct EU farm set-aside.

text.p: If recent rain continues it could hit crop prospects and increase the likelihood that 1998 cereals set-aside would be unchanged at five percent, a senior European Commission agriculture source said on Monday.

After a long dry spell in much of Europe, rain initially raised expectations of an even bigger harvest than the record 202 million tonnes of 1996. Another record crop would fuel demands to curb production and prevent grain mountains reappearing.
"That's not so likely now," the source said, adding this year's crop would probably be a little smaller.

With intervention grain stocks very low at less than two million tonnes, Commission sources note little safety margin in the event of harvest "hiccups" which would thus make it difficult to raise set-aside and curb production.
Despite total production around 200 million tonnes "useable" output could be much lower if quality suffered due to wet weather, an industry source said.
The Commission source cautioned that last year the harvest estimate jumped some 11 million tonnes in a few days following good weather at a crucial time.
Last week in Luxembourg, EU farm ministers called for unchanged set-aside. But EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler would not be rushed into making a proposal until he had more crop data.
He is expected to recommend a rate in time for a formal decision at the next EU farm ministers' meeting on July 22. -Brussels bureau +322 287 6830
